questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.**

The poor undergoes several problems in life that could be solved with money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**The poor undergoes**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in the original sentence arises from a **subject-verb agreement** issue.
 
• The subject "**the poor**" is a plural noun phrase, but the verb "**undergoes**" is in the singular form.
 
• In English, verbs must agree in number with their subjects.
 
• So, "**The poor undergo**" should be corrected to "**The poor undergo**".
 
• The correct form would be "The poor undergo," where the verb "undergo" is in the plural form to match the plural subject "the poor."
 
• 
 
The **correct sentence** should be: "*The poor undergo several problems in life that could be solved with money.*"

 
 
• 
 
In this corrected version, "**undergo**" is used correctly with the plural noun "**problems**," and the verb "**undergo**" agrees with the plural subject "**the poor.**"

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Can you please tell me __where__ __is the city park ?__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**where the city park is?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The overall structure of the sentence is an **interrogative sentence**, starting with the auxiliary verb **"can"**.
 
• It's asking someone else to provide information. An embedded indirect question "where the city park is" is used, and this follows English rule of structure for indirect questions.
 
• In indirect questions or embedded questions, the usual word order of a statement is kept. That's why we use "where the city park is" instead of "where is the city park?" which is how the question would be posed directly.
 
• The **subject** (the city park) precedes the** auxiliary verb** (is) in indirect questions, hence 'where the city park is' is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Can you please tell me where the city park is ?***

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The Indian army airlifted thousands of people from Ukraine.

options.text: Thousands of people had been airlifted from Ukraine by the Indian army.
Thousands of people have been airlifted from Ukraine by the Indian army.
Thousands of people are airlifted from Ukraine by the Indian army.
Thousands of people were airlifted from Ukraine by the Indian army.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**Thousands of people were airlifted from Ukraine by the Indian army.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject, and the original subject often becomes the agent (or is omitted).
 
• The structure generally follows the pattern:
 
 
• 
 
**Active Voice**: Subject + Verb + Object + Additional information__

 
 
• 
 
**Passive Voice**: __Object + Was/were + V3 + by + agent + additional information__

 
 
 
 
• The subject in the active voice sentence, "**The Indian army,**" becomes the agent in the passive voice construction.
 
• It is placed at the end of the sentence preceded by "**by**."
 
• The object in the active voice sentence, "**thousands of people**," becomes the subject in the passive voice construction.
 
• The verb "**airlifted**" changes to "**were airlifted**" in the passive voice, indicating the past participle.
 
• So, the passive construction maintains the same essential information but shifts the focus from the doer of the action (the Indian army) to the receiver of the action (thousands of people).

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:

• We use the modal verb "**can**" to indicate ability.
 
• The sentence becomes: "*Who can solve the problem?*"
